test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A pair of parallel lines is intersected by a transversal such that ∠1 and ∠2 form a pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal. If m ∠1 = 125°, what is the measure of ∠2?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **parallel lines** intersected by a **transversal**, the sum of **consecutive interior angles** (interior angles on the same side) is always 180°.

Measure of ∠2 = 180° − Measure of ∠1

⇒ ∠2 = 180° − 125° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lines are **parallel**.

∠1 and ∠2 are **interior angles** on the **same side of the transversal**.

m∠1 = 125°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5843f869c6eeca7b139d9a1970a1a80c1aa4931a312d7c91abe4d51fb8fd493f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

When two **parallel lines** are cut by a **transversal**, the **consecutive interior angles** are **supplementary**.

m∠1 + m∠2 = 180°

**Calculations:**

⇒ 125° + m∠2 = 180°

⇒ m∠2 = 180° − 125°

⇒ m∠2 = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. If the lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal. These angles are always equal when lines are parallel.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles whose measures sum up to 180° are called supplementary angles.</p
